summary: Discovery-style security review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model for a regulated healthcare customer. Covered SAML flows, SCIM attribute mappings, RBAC roles and custom roles, audit logging, KMS/encryption model, and compliance artifacts (SOC 2/ISO). Agreed next steps: share implementation docs, schedule technical deep-dive, provide IdP metadata.

SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and scoping for Crest
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (Crest Head of Security), Tom (IT Ops), Amir (CTO), Sophie (Compliance)

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can folks see my screen? Uh, just a quick -- we're going to run through SSO/SCIM and RBAC at a high level then dig into any specifics you want.
[00:14] Lena: Yeah we can see it. Thanks Evan. For context, Crest is doing a security review because we're looking at private deployment first, but we want Hosted with VPC too as an option.
[00:28] Priya: Great, thanks Lena. Quick agenda: SAML SSO flow, SCIM provisioning, RBAC/least-privilege patterns, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS, then compliance artifacts (SOC 2 / ISO). We'll pause for questions.
[00:42] Tom: Sounds good. Our main concerns: ensure least privilege for devs vs ops, SCIM mapping to AD groups, and that audit logs capture admin activity for compliance. Also data residency questions.
[00:58] Evan: Got it. Priya, can you run the SAML diagram?
[01:03] Priya: Yep. So standard SAML 2.0 flow: IdP initiated or SP initiated supported. We exchange IdP metadata (entityID, x509 cert, ACS URL). For Hosted customers the ACS is redwood-hosted domain; for Private/VPC deployments we provide a customer-specific ACS endpoint.
[01:24] Lena: For Crest we're using Okta, but we also have a subset on Azure AD. We plan to do Okta first. We need SCIM to provision users and deprovision quickly.
[01:36] Priya: Okta is a common flow. SCIM 2.0 support includes group push. We recommend using the group-to-role mapping: push your AD/Okta groups, then map groups to Redwood roles.
[01:50] Amir: How do custom roles work? We need a role that has read-only embed access for analytics team, and another that can create models but not manage billing.
[02:01] Priya: We support system roles and custom roles. System roles are Admin, Developer, Viewer, Billing. Custom roles can be created in the Console; you pick allowed actions like model.deploy, route.invoke, billing.view. We'll demo that in the deep-dive.
[02:16] Tom: Is role creation auditable? We need to show who created or changed a role for SOC2 evidence.
[02:22] Priya: Yes, all admin actions are logged in the audit log with actor, timestamp, IP, and request payload. Logs can be exported to your SIEM via Syslog or delivered to your customer-owned S3 bucket.
[02:36] Sophie: Retention? We need 12 months for some artifacts.
[02:40] Evan: We have configurable retention policies; default is 90 days on hosted but enterprise plans can set longer retention and we can push to your S3 for long-term storage. We'll include retention SLAs in the contract.
[02:51] Lena: How about least-privilege recommendations? We're trying to avoid giving devs billing or infra rights.
[02:59] Priya: Recommendation: use SCIM to create groups corresponding to environment and function (e.g., prod-developers, prod-viewers, infra-admins). Map groups to least-privilege roles: prod-developers -> deploy.invoke but not billing.*, infra-admins -> infra.* but not billing.view, billing-admins -> billing.* only. Also separate keys: don't hand out account-level API keys to developers—issue scoped API keys tied to a role and route, with TTL.
[03:23] Amir: Scoped API keys? Can you explain TTL and rotation?
[03:27] Priya: Sure. Keys can be short-lived (hours/days) for developers; we support automated rotation and can integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption. For long-lived service tokens, those are typically minted for CI/CD and stored in your secret manager. We also support mTLS for private deployment.
[03:44] Lena: On the KMS side, do you support customer-managed keys? We need CMEK for certain data at rest requirements.
[03:50] Priya: Yes, for Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM). For Hosted we offer optional Bring-Your-Own-Key where the key is in your KMS and we use envelope encryption; Redwood never stores your plaintext key.
[04:06] Tom: Are model weights encrypted at rest as well?
[04:09] Priya: We encrypt all stored artifacts at rest using AES-256; with CMEK we wrap the data key with your KMS. There are some operational notes for large artifact encryption but functionally it's covered.
[04:20] Lena: Audit logs again — what about admin console logins via SSO?
[04:24] Priya: Those are logged as auth events (success/failure) including SAML assertions metadata where available. We include the user identifier, IdP, and assertion ID when present. For deeper context we'll include correlation IDs so your SIEM can link SAML events to subsequent API actions.
[04:40] Sophie: For SOC 2: are you willing to provide the SOC 2 Type II report and associated control narratives?
[04:45] Evan: Yes, we provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs under NDA. We'll share the package with your security team after the NDA is in place.
[04:55] Lena: Also need to confirm data residency. Crest has PHI that must remain in us-east-1. Does hosted support region pinning?
[05:04] Priya: We support region pinning for data residency for enterprise customers; we can pin storage and inference nodes to a specific cloud region. For Private deployments it's naturally in your region.
[05:16] Tom: Good. On SCIM mapping—what attributes do you expect from our IdP? We use custom attributes like employeeNumber and costCenter.
[05:26] Priya: SCIM requires core: userName, name, emails, and groups. We support mapping custom attributes; we can map employeeNumber -> user.external_id and costCenter -> custom attribute on the user. We'll share a sample SCIM mapping template.
[05:42] Amir: How do group renames or deletions propagate? We need safe deprovisioning patterns.
[05:49] Priya: For delete events SCIM can send a DELETE for the user; for groups we support group removal. Our recommendation: use deactivation first then delete after a grace period. We also support webhook hooks so you can be notified of SCIM events.
[06:05] Lena: Anything about provisioning speed of SCIM? We have 5k users.
[06:09] Priya: SCIM is paginated and we handle bulk operations; initial sync of 5k users typically completes in a few minutes, depending on IdP rate limits. For very large orgs we can do a staged sync. We'll run a pilot.
[06:22] Tom: Can we require MFA on Redwood console logins enforced by IdP?
[06:26] Priya: Yes, MFA is enforced at the IdP level via SAML. Redwood respects the assertion and does not override MFA. For programmatic access, we recommend short-lived tokens plus rotation via your secrets manager.
[06:38] Sophie: Regarding RBAC, do you have built-in role templates for healthcare (HIPAA) or do we need to design from scratch?
[06:46] Priya: We provide templates: Healthcare Viewer, Healthcare Admin, Researcher (restricted), etc. Those are starting points you can customize. We'll share the template docs.
[06:58] Evan: Quick Q from me — Crest is asking about separation of duties: can we ensure billing admins can't spin up inference clusters?
[07:07] Priya: Yes, separation is enforced via privileges. Billing roles only expose billing.* endpoints. Cluster provisioning is part of infra.* or platform-admin roles. Also we recommend using RBAC + approval workflows in the Console for large infra changes.
[07:22] Lena: Do approval workflows create an audit trail?
[07:25] Priya: Yes, approvals are recorded as admin actions in the audit log with approver identity and comment.
[07:31] Tom: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for some events.
[07:36] Priya: We produce logs with cryptographic hashes on request and can stream to your S3 where you control immutability/lock policies. For higher assurance we can work with your security team on an HSM-backed signing process.
[07:49] Amir: Encryption in transit — TLS? Any client cert pinning?
[07:53] Priya: TLS 1.2+ enforced. For Private we support mutual TLS for node-to-node and client-to-gateway. Additionally, we support IP allowlists and VPC peering.
[08:05] Lena: A few nitty gritty items: SAML NameID format — do you require email? We have some service accounts that use username only.
[08:15] Priya: We prefer email but can accept persistent NameID or an attribute (like user.email). We'll document acceptable NameID formats. For service accounts we recommend provisioning via SCIM with a service principal flag.
[08:30] Sophie: For compliance review we'll need sample logs showing a role change, a provisioning event, and a data access event. Can you provide examples?
[08:38] Evan: Yup — we can provide redacted sample logs for those events. We'll attach them to the SOC package under NDA.
[08:46] Tom: Any known gaps for health data — HIPAA? I know SOC2 covers controls, but do you sign a BAA?
[08:53] Evan: We do sign BAAs for healthcare customers on enterprise agreements. We'll route this to legal after you confirm deployment mode.
[09:02] Lena: Ok good. A question about SCIM group-to-role mapping complexity: if a user is in multiple groups, which role wins?
[09:10] Priya: We evaluate privileges by union: the user's effective permissions are the union of all group-mapped roles; for conflicts where you need strict isolation we recommend separate accounts or an enforcement layer. We can also support precedence rules on group mapping if you need exclusivity.
[09:28] Amir: Does Redwood expose a test endpoint to validate SAML assertions during setup?
[09:33] Priya: Yes, we have a SAML test endpoint and a diagnostic view in Console showing parsed assertions and SCIM sync logs. It helps debug mapping issues live.
[09:44] Tom: Good to know. On monitoring and alerts — can we send alerts for anomalous admin activity?
[09:50] Priya: Yes, you can configure alerting for admin events, failed logins, large-volume API calls, model-rollouts, etc. Alerts can go to your pager or to a Slack webhook.
[09:59] Sophie: One more — retention of SAML assertions for forensic tracebacks.
[10:03] Priya: We keep assertions for 30 days by default; extended retention is possible if you push them to your S3.
[10:11] Evan: We're close to time — let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:15] Lena: Quick note — any limits on SCIM attributes length/types?
[10:19] Priya: We'll include that in the SCIM mapping doc; generally string fields up to 1024 bytes, and we support boolean/number types.
[10:27] Evan: Recap: Evan will share SAML/SCIM implementation docs and sample logs; Priya will schedule a technical deep-dive and demo of the RBAC console; Tom will send IdP metadata and group lists; Crest to confirm hosted vs private decision and BAA needs.
[10:44] Sophie: Thanks everyone.
[10:46] Evan: Thanks — we'll follow up via email with attachments.
[10:49] Priya: Thanks all, talk soon.
